result.summary:
1) READ the test in full (engine_sub_process_test.exs:1264-1330) and TEST-DESIGNER's handoff (step-04-test-designer.json). Confirmed the single test's 6 assertions each map to a distinct acceptance-criterion facet: no Multi crash (line 1287), root instance reaches :completed (1294), both sibling children created with correct parent linkage (1300-1306), both SUB_PROCESS_COMPLETED events fired (1310), zero orphan task rows (1318), and join_counters cleared post-join (1328, cross-referenced with ISS-0397). No `@tag :skip`, no 'TODO: implement test' anywhere in the file. Fixtures use `provisioned_tenant()` (fresh schema per test), `active_definition!/2` scoped to that schema, `unique_idempotency_key/1`, and `Ecto.UUID.generate()` -- no shared mutable state, no cross-test ordering dependency, no hardcoded secrets/connection strings anywhere in the diff or test file.

2) INDEPENDENT MUTATION REPRODUCTION (mandatory, since this is a WF-03 regression test and the pre-fix baseline here is 'a different, wrong key shape existed,' not 'the module didn't exist' -- so the stricter does-the-test-exist-not-existing case doesn't strictly apply, but I reproduced one mutation myself regardless for direct, non-copied evidence). Read sub_process.ex:960-974 and task_activation.ex:265-298 myself and confirmed the exact mechanism TEST-DESIGNER described: `append_multi_from_existing_records/7`'s `key_disambiguator \\ nil` defaults the Multi key to `{:task_records, instance_id}` when omitted, and only becomes `{:task_records, instance_id, disambiguator}` when `parent_token.id` is passed. I judged mutation (a) -- dropping the `parent_token.id` argument at sub_process.ex:967-974 -- the most load-bearing of the three (it is literally ISS-0396's own root cause: the un-disambiguated key collision) and reproduced it myself:
   - Applied: removed the trailing `parent_token.id` arg from the `TaskActivation.append_multi_from_existing_records` call at sub_process.ex:967-974.
   - Ran `mix test test/letflow/engine_sub_process_test.exs`. Real output: `Result: 15/16 passed` with failure `** (RuntimeError) cannot merge Multi; the following operations were found in both Ecto.Multi: [task_records: "58c094e3-3402-40c0-894c-56f5fa19f14f"]` -- byte-for-byte the same collision shape (unqualified `{:task_records, instance_id}` key, no disambiguator tuple element) that both the design doc and TEST-DESIGNER's own handoff describe as the pre-fix failure.
   - Reverted: `git checkout -- lib/letflow/engine/sub_process.ex`. Confirmed `git status --porcelain lib/ test/` produced no output (clean tree, no residual diff).
   - Re-ran `mix test test/letflow/engine_sub_process_test.exs`: `Result: 16 passed`, 0 failures -- suite restored to green.
   This independently confirms (not merely re-states) that the test genuinely discriminates the fixed key-disambiguation logic from the pre-fix collision, matching TEST-DESIGNER's mutation (a) claim exactly.

3) FLAGGED FINDING REVIEW (TaskActivation.append_multi_from_existing_records/7 vs. Transition.dispatch_parallel_join/4's synthetic token id): read transition.ex:1196-1218 myself and confirmed `fire_join/5` mints `new_token_id = counter.origin_token_id <> "/" <> node.id <> "/joined"` -- a synthetic, non-UUID string -- for the freshly-joined branch's continuation token. Read task_activation.ex:300-331 and confirmed `insert_newly_pending_from_existing_records/5` calls `cast_token_record_id/1`, which runs the token_id through `Ecto.UUID.cast/1` and returns `{:error, {:invalid_token_record_id, token_id}}` on any non-UUID string -- which `"<uuid>/join/joined"` is. This independently verifies the defect is real. Read the design doc (iss0396-task-records-multi-sibling-fix.md) myself: §5's own test-scope list only requires join->END (line 312-315, 'advancing the root instance straight through join to end... nothing here is gated behind a HUMAN_TASK'), and §5's explicit out-of-scope note (line 353-357) only excludes the complete_task/3-triggered variant, not a join-then-further-work variant -- but the whole document's own worked example, both `OQ` items, and the shipped test all only exercise join->END. TEST-DESIGNER's own handoff and gate_history confirm the exploratory join->HUMAN_TASK test and its helper graph were reverted (`git diff --stat test/letflow/engine_sub_process_test.exs` empty per their report); I independently confirmed the current working tree's test file has no such helper graph or describe block beyond the one at line 1264, and `git status --porcelain` is clean on this branch as delivered. This finding is genuinely pre-existing, ISS-0396-unrelated (it is about `TaskActivation`/`Transition`'s general join-continuation contract, not about the `:task_records` Multi-key collision ISS-0396 fixes), correctly out of this test's coverage obligation, and was correctly NOT merged as a failing/skipped test -- TEST-DESIGNER handled it exactly right (revert clean, flag for ORCH, no self-filed issue id per the ISSUE_QUEUE.md protocol).

4) FINAL VERIFICATION (my own run, post-revert, on the branch exactly as delivered): `mix test test/letflow/engine_sub_process_test.exs` -> `Finished in 20.6 seconds` / `Result: 16 passed`, 0 failures. `git status --porcelain` empty both before and after my mutation-and-revert cycle -- no uncommitted changes left in the tree.

All TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR checks pass: every acceptance-criterion facet has runnable, non-vacuous coverage; no skip/TODO; fixtures self-sufficient and isolated; no hardcoded secrets; and I have now independently reproduced (not merely read) one of the three claimed pre-fix mutation failures, matching TEST-DESIGNER's reported evidence exactly.
